ground_truth: Linear data structures operating on opposite ordering principles: Stacks follow Last-In-First-Out (LIFO), whereas Queues follow First-In-First-Out (FIFO).
pre_quiz: In what order are elements removed from a stack compared to a queue?
pre_quiz_answer: A stack removes the most recently added item (LIFO), while a queue removes the oldest added item (FIFO).
post_quiz: Which data structure is naturally used to model function call returns in a CPU?
post_quiz_answer: A call stack, because the most recently called function must finish before returning to the caller.
